title: the suites pass on the runners CI uses, and the local sweep sees what those runners see
description: CI failed on the pushed main for causes the local sweep could not see: environment inputs it passes through (the session variables, git's system config and identity guessing, the installed shells) and a report-coverage gap the dogfood plan's own data triggered. Fix each cause red first by flipping the input that hid it, then close the class in the sweep and in verify.sh.
desiredOutcome: CI's ubuntu selftests and manifest-validation jobs are green on the phase's head, and the local sweep, run in the environment it now isolates, fails on each cause they failed on before the fix

findings.issue: The heredoc reader also matches a here-string (<<<), reads its word as a terminator and drops every following line, so a checker call after a here-string vanishes from the target set with no finding.
findings.resolution: fixed in P92.6-a1x (67aac9f3): Match a heredoc only on exactly two angle brackets; a case puts a here-string before a real call and asserts the call is read.

findings.issue: The target keeps trailing shell punctuation, so a call written as `if ... ; then` on one side and bare on the other reads as a missing document.
findings.resolution: fixed in P92.6-a1x (67aac9f3): Tokenise with shell punctuation separated; an allow case with the same target in both spellings.

findings.issue: The comment says the mutation reports every rendered leg missing; it actually leaves the scratch root unexpanded, which the reader reports as an unresolved target.
findings.resolution: fixed in P92.6-a1x (67aac9f3): Say what the mutation does.

findings.file: tools/gate-parity.py; tools/sweep-selftests.py (comments and a case label)
findings.issue: Present-tense counts of what the files hold (legs from the generator's tree, documents in a loop, names outside the prefix) go wrong when one is added.
findings.resolution: fixed in P92.6-a1x (67aac9f3): Delete the numbers and keep the pointers.

findings.issue: The filtered isolation families are named in three documents that nothing checks; the documents say so, but it is a rule in prose in documents this repo has recorded drifting apart.
findings.resolution: fixed in P92.6-a1x (67aac9f3): isolation_drift derives the filtered families from the runner's constants and requires each document to name them; then drop the sentences that say nothing checks them.

tasks.title: a case skipped on one platform and run on another is one case, not a duplicate id
tasks.description: The harness records a call site as a bare line number and skip() calls check() from inside the harness, so test__refs lr2 (run on one shell, skipped where zsh is absent) reads as a duplicate on ubuntu and windows. A skip registers no call site of its own; sites are keyed by the file and line of the first frame outside the harness. Red first by making zsh unavailable to the case.

add: plugins/audit/tests/_harness.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a case run through check() on one branch and through skip() on another is reported as a duplicate case id

outcome.technical: _harness._call_site: a skip registers no site; a site is the file and line of the first frame outside the harness; label_faults reports basename:line; cases cs1-cs4.
outcome.descriptive: A case skipped where a shell is absent and run where it exists keeps one id, and two real call sites under one id are still reported, now even across files sharing a line number.

intentCheck.basis: the harness fix the diagnosis named

tasks.title: the lock and branch fixtures in test_audit_task hold on a runner with no session and a plain git
tasks.description: k1-k4: the fixture takes the lock in the test's own process, whose token then rides in AUDIT_LOCK_TOKENS and lets the verb back in when no session variable names another caller (CI). Take the fixture lock from a subprocess, or drop the carried token, and pin the session variables the case means. tw5/tw6: mk() and mk_pair_empty() run git init without a branch, which is main only under Apple git's system config; use an explicit initial branch. Red first with the session variables stripped and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: repro that FAILS on current code - with the Claude session variables stripped and git's system config ignored, k1-k4 and tw5/tw6 fail

outcome.technical: k-group fixture lock taken by a child process with session variables unset for the group; git init -q -b main in mk() and mk_pair_empty(); tw0.
outcome.descriptive: The lock cases no longer depend on the runner's Claude session variables, and the git fixtures start on main whatever the runner's default branch.

intentCheck.basis: the fixture fixes the diagnosis named, plus a case for the fixture no case read

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_close_phase.py: repro that FAILS on current code - with identity guessing refused, mh2's --no-ff merge cannot commit

outcome.technical: _init_fixture_repo: git init -b main and a repo-local identity, used by every fixture in test_close_phase.
outcome.descriptive: close-phase's merge cases no longer depend on the host being able to guess a git identity.

CI's one-status leg renders the live dogfood plan while its comment says the plan is all one status: render a committed fixture that is, or say what it renders. verify.sh runs the same rendered-plan legs as ci.yml so a local green covers them.

tasks.title: the sweep hands its suites no ambient session or git configuration, so a local green means what CI's does
tasks.description: The class behind the ubuntu failures: the sweep isolates cwd, TMPDIR, HOME/XDG and the pycache but passes the rest of the environment through. For every child: drop the Claude session variables (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_PID and the rest of that family), ignore git's system configuration (GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM), and refuse git's identity guessing (user.useConfigOnly) with no default branch pinned, so a suite that leans on the host's git fails here the way it fails on a bare runner rather than passing under a pinned default. A sweep case fails if any of these reaches a child. Name the new families where isolation_drift reads them (CLAUDE.md's Tests paragraph, CONTRIBUTING.md and fixture_root's docstring). Prove it red first: with P92.1-P92.4 reverted in a scratch tree, the isolated sweep fails on exactly the causes CI failed on.

add: tools/sweep-selftests.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a child suite sees a Claude session variable, git's system configuration, or a git identity guessed from the host

outcome.technical: tools/sweep-selftests.py: ambient_env drops the CLAUDE_ prefix, CLAUDECODE, AUDIT_LOCK_TOKENS and git's documented identity names, and sets GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM and user.useConfigOnly; no branch or identity pinned; cases se0-se5, x8-x14. CLAUDE.md Tests paragraph, CONTRIBUTING.md isolation block and fixture_root's docstring name the filtered families and state that isolation_drift does not read them.
outcome.descriptive: A local sweep hands its suites the bare session and git a CI runner has: no Claude session variables, no system git configuration, no guessed or exported git identity; over the pre-fix tree it now fails on the suites whose CI failure came from the environment (the lock, branch and identity fixtures); the duplicate-id failure, which depends on which shells a machine has installed, is held on every platform by the harness's own cases instead.

intentCheck.basis: the isolation the diagnosis named, widened to ambient git identity, with the class proved on the pre-fix tree

tasks.title: the report-target reader reads every call the shell would run, and the filtered isolation families are held in the documents by a check
tasks.description: Phase review fix task. report_target_drift: a heredoc is matched on exactly two angle brackets so a here-string does not swallow the lines after it; a call's first argument is read with shell punctuation separated so an if/then spelling and a bare one agree. prove-gates' rt2 comment says what its mutation does. Present-tense counts in the new comments and a case label become pointers. isolation_drift also derives the filtered families (the session prefix and names, the git identity names, the git configuration it sets) from sweep-selftests.py and requires each isolation document to name them; the sentences saying nothing checks them go.

add: tools/gate-parity.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a checker call after a here-string vanishes from the target set, and a document that stops naming a filtered isolation family passes

outcome.technical: gate-parity.py: two-bracket heredoc match, shlex.shlex with punctuation_chars and whitespace_split, filtered_env_families/_covers/uncovered_members in isolation_drift; prove-gates rows for the new drift and a corrected rt2 comment; counts in prose removed; CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md describe the check.
outcome.descriptive: The report-target reader no longer loses a call after a here-string or reads shell punctuation into a file name, and every name the sweep filters is held, as a code span, to each document that describes the isolation.
